firmware.summary:
A few fixes and one new Victron device supported.

The button on the back now changes screens — quick press for the next one, hold for a couple of seconds to turn the WiFi setup on or off. (Don't hold it while powering up.)
Warning flashing can be turned off — from the settings menu on screen, or the WiFi page.
No more picking up the neighbours — it now locks on to your own Victron gear and ignores everyone else's.
Victron VE.Bus Smart Dongle supported — for MultiPlus owners, on the Battery Sense screen.
More batteries recognised — some lithium batteries with Daly-type management that never connected now work.

Worth updating if you've had odd readings in a busy campsite, or a battery that never showed up. Otherwise it'll keep.
firmware.changes:
ChargeScreen 10.22

The button on the back now changes screens. There are two small buttons on the rear of the unit — one of them just resets the device, the other is the function button. A quick press on the function button moves you to the next screen, so you can flick through without reaching up and touching the glass. Hold it down for a couple of seconds and it turns the WiFi setup hotspot on or off.

You can turn the warning flashing off. If ChargeScreen jumping to a screen and flashing at you every time Victron reports a warning is more nuisance than help, you can now switch it off. Either from the settings menu on the screen itself, or from the WiFi setup page. Your readings all carry on as normal, it just stops interrupting you.

Your screen won't pick up the neighbours any more. If you've been parked near other vans or boats with Victron equipment, there was a small chance ChargeScreen would grab a reading from their gear instead of yours . A voltage that jumped oddly, or a figure that didn't match what VictronConnect was telling you. It now locks on to your own equipment the first time it sees it and ignores everything else. If a device is switched off or moved out of range it lets go again, so swapping a unit still works as before.

Victron MultiPlus owners with the VE.Bus Smart Dongle can now see it on the Battery Sense screen. Voltage, temperature and any warnings. Same as the other Victron devices: pop the key in from VictronConnect and it appears.

More batteries recognised. Some lithium batteries using Daly-type battery management wouldn't connect at all and just sat there saying nothing. ChargeScreen now tries a second way of talking to them, which picks up a number of batteries that previously didn't work.

Plus the usual tidying under the bonnet.

Current bugs.
Few users are reporting issues with eco-worthy. This has been a bit of a pain to sort out, but really want to get this sorted. Made worse by the fact my brother in law's eco worthy works fine, but some customer's dont.
I think the issue stems from eco-worthy using different BMS's and putting their badge on it.

instructions.power: Power ChargeScreen using USB-C, or if you bought a rear power supply cable, carefully plug it in and make sure the notch on the cable lines up with the gap on the plug.
instructions.victron_intro: ChargeScreen reads Victron Instant Readout Bluetooth adverts. Those adverts are encrypted, so each Victron device needs its own Instant Readout encryption data.
instructions.victron_first_step: Open the VictronConnect app near your Victron device.
instructions.ble_intro: BLE capture records nearby Bluetooth Low Energy adverts for 5 minutes. It is useful when adding support for batteries or accessories that do not decode correctly yet.
instructions.ble_privacy: Privacy note: the CSV may include packets from nearby watches, phones, TVs, sensors, and batteries. Most of it is encrypted or only useful to the original device, but it will still appear in the file. Battery encryption codes are only used to decode the battery packets in the capture.
